newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas called steady ahead of storage data.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas called steady ahead of storage data.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open on either side of unchanged Wednesday following a steady ACCESS session and ahead of the weekly storage data due later today, industry sources said.
June over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.18 to $2.20 after settling Tuesday at $2.191 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, June wavered between $2.19 and $2.22 and last traded 0.8 cent higher at $2.199.
Injection estimates for today's weekly AGA storage report range from 50 to 75 bcf, versus a gain of 59 bcf a year ago.
Technical traders said support in June was at $2.15 and then at $2.05. Resistance was pegged at $2.30 and then at the $2.43 contract high.

In Tuesday's cash, Gulf Coast swing prices slipped a few cents to the high-teens. Midcon pipes were down slightly to about $2.00. New York city gate gas was quoted about five cents lower in the mid-$2.40s.
Helping to keep a lid on cash prices were forecasts for a continuation of cooler-than-normal weather in the Northeast, Midwest and Texas through early next week, according to Weather Services Corp.
However, maintenance on Transco's Texas line will continue to cut about 400 mmcfd out of a total capacity of about 600 mmcfd through Thursday.

Also, planned work on Mobil's Mary Ann gas processing plant in Coden, Ala., has cut the plant's total processing capacity of 380-390 mmcfd. About 120 mmcfd should be back within the next seven days, with the balance due back in three weeks.
